text: The applicant, Genderdoc-M, is a non-governmental organisation based in Moldova.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant, Genderdoc-M, has as its object to provide information and to assist the LGBT community.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 7 April 2005, the applicant association applied to Chişinău Municipal Council for authorisation to hold a peaceful demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The peaceful demonstration for which the applicant association sought authorisation was to be held in front of the Parliament on 27 May 2005.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The purpose of the proposed demonstration was to encourage the adoption of laws to protect sexual minorities from discrimination.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 27 April 2005, the Chişinău Municipal Council rejected the applicant association's application to hold a demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Municipal Council rejected the application on the ground that the applicant association's demonstration was baseless.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Municipal Council stated as justification that a law on the protection of national minorities had already been adopted.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 6 May 2005, the Chişinău Mayor's Office refused permission for the proposed demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Mayor's Office refused permission on the ground that a law on the protection of national minorities was already in place.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Mayor's Office also refused permission on the ground that there were legal provisions which dictated which individuals had the power of legislative initiative required to promote laws.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant association contested the decision of the Chişinău Mayor's Office of 6 May 2005.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant association argued that the ban on their demonstration was illegal.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant association argued that the ban on their demonstration was discriminatory.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 2 June 2005, the Chişinău Court of Appeal allowed the applicant association's action.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 2 June 2005, the Chişinău Court of Appeal declared the Chişinău Mayor's Office decision of 6 May 2005 void.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Court of Appeal found that the arguments relied on by the Chişinău Mayor's Office to justify its refusal to authorise the assembly were legally ungrounded, as the law does not provide such grounds for the non-authorisation of an assembly.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Court of Appeal found that the decision as to whether to authorise or not to authorise an assembly should not be made conditional on the nature of the problems the participants intend to bring to society's attention.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Court of Appeal found that the decision as to whether to authorise or not to authorise an assembly should not be made conditional on the status of those problems.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Court of Appeal concluded that the Chişinău Mayor's Office decision of 6 May 2005 was issued contrary to the provisions of Article 26(1) of the Law regarding administrative complaints, and was thus illegal and void.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Court of Appeal declared ill-founded the applicant association's complaint regarding the Chişinău Mayor's Office's non-compliance with the time-limit of forty-eight hours for notification of the refusal of authorisation for the assembly required under section 14 of the Law regarding the organisation and conduct of assemblies.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Mayor's Office appealed against the decision of the Chişinău Court of Appeal of 2 June 2005.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Chişinău Mayor's Office argued that they had received many requests from individuals and associations which were vehemently against the authorisation of the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The individuals and associations who sent requests to the Chişinău Mayor's Office opposed the adoption of any law legalising homosexual partnerships.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The requests received by the Chişinău Mayor's Office laid emphasis on various legal provisions that concerned the protection of marriage and the family.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 7 September 2005, the Supreme Court of Justice of Moldova allowed the appeal lodged by the Chişinău Mayor's Office.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 7 September 2005, the Supreme Court of Justice of Moldova quashed the Chişinău Court of Appeal decision of 2 June 2005.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 7 September 2005, the Supreme Court of Justice of Moldova decided to send the case to the Chişinău Court of Appeal for re-examination.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In their submissions to the Chişinău Court of Appeal on re-examination, the Chişinău Mayor's Office argued that the holding of an assembly for the promotion of the rights of sexual minorities would endanger public order.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In their submissions to the Chişinău Court of Appeal on re-examination, the Chişinău Mayor's Office argued that the holding of an assembly for the promotion of the rights of sexual minorities would endanger social morality.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In their submissions to the Chişinău Court of Appeal on re-examination, the Chişinău Mayor's Office argued that the organisers of the demonstration had not assumed any responsibility as regards the demonstration's good management.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant association argued before the Chişinău Court of Appeal on re-examination that the ban on their demonstration was illegal.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant association argued before the Chişinău Court of Appeal on re-examination that the ban on their demonstration was discriminatory.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 14 June 2006, the Chişinău Court of Appeal found against the applicant association on re-examination.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant association appealed against the Chişinău Court of Appeal decision of 14 June 2006.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 18 October 2006, the Supreme Court of Justice of Moldova upheld the decision of the Chişinău Court of Appeal of 14 June 2006.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Supreme Court of Justice of Moldova found that the applicant association had failed to give undertakings to respect the law, as required by law in respect of assemblies.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Supreme Court of Justice of Moldova found that the applicant association had failed to give undertakings to designate a person or persons in charge of the conduct of the demonstration, as required by law in respect of assemblies.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Supreme Court of Justice of Moldova found that the applicant association had failed to give undertakings to create together with the police a group of people responsible for the maintenance of public order, as required by law in respect of assemblies.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Supreme Court of Justice of Moldova found that the applicant association had failed to give undertakings to mark the site of the demonstration with special signs, as required by law in respect of assemblies.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Supreme Court of Justice of Moldova found that the applicant association had failed to give undertakings to pay the Chişinău Municipal Council any fees related to the arrangement of the site of the demonstration, as required by law in respect of assemblies.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Supreme Court of Justice of Moldova found that the applicant association had failed to give undertakings to establish the route to and from the site of the demonstration, as required by law in respect of assemblies.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Supreme Court of Justice of Moldova found that the applicant association had failed to give undertakings to provide the police with unfettered access to the site of the demonstration, as required by law in respect of assemblies.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Supreme Court of Justice of Moldova found that the applicant association had failed to give undertakings to forbid the participation of certain persons, as required by law in respect of assemblies.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Supreme Court of Justice of Moldova considered that there was a risk that the demonstration would cause a breach of public order.

text: Law no. 560-XIII of 21 July 1995 regarding the organisation and conduct of assemblies provides under Section 5 that assemblies may be held only after the organisers have duly notified the urban mayor's (municipal) or rural offices.

Law no. 560-XIII of 21 July 1995 regarding the organisation and conduct of assemblies provides under Section 11(1) that the organiser of an assembly must lodge a notification with the mayor's office at least fifteen days before the chosen date, according to the model provided in the appendix to that law.

Law no. 560-XIII of 21 July 1995 regarding the organisation and conduct of assemblies provides under Section 11(2) that the preliminary notification should indicate the name of the organiser and the aim of the assembly.

Law no. 560-XIII of 21 July 1995 regarding the organisation and conduct of assemblies provides under Section 11(2) that the preliminary notification should indicate the date and time the assembly is to begin and end.

Law no. 560-XIII of 21 July 1995 regarding the organisation and conduct of assemblies provides under Section 11(2) that the preliminary notification should indicate where the assembly will take place and the routes to and from the place.
Law no. 560-XIII of 21 July 1995 regarding the organisation and conduct of assemblies provides under Section 11(2) that the preliminary notification should indicate the form the assembly will take.

Law no. 560-XIII of 21 July 1995 regarding the organisation and conduct of assemblies provides under Section 11(2) that the preliminary notification should indicate the approximate number of participants.

Law no. 560-XIII of 21 July 1995 regarding the organisation and conduct of assemblies provides under Section 11(2) that the preliminary notification should indicate those appointed to ensure the good conduct of the assembly and to be responsible for it.

Law no. 560-XIII of 21 July 1995 regarding the organisation and conduct of assemblies provides under Section 11(2) that the preliminary notification should indicate the services the organisers require from the mayor's office.

Law no. 560-XIII of 21 July 1995 regarding the organisation and conduct of assemblies provides under Section 11(3) that the Mayor's Office may in justified cases modify, with the organiser's consent, elements of the preliminary notification.

Law no. 560-XIII of 21 July 1995 regarding the organisation and conduct of assemblies provides under Section 13 that after examining the preliminary declaration, the Mayor's Office shall issue one of the following decisions and inform the organiser: grant permission, or refuse permission under section 12(6).
Law no. 560-XIII of 21 July 1995 regarding the organisation and conduct of assemblies provides under Section 15(1) that the organiser can contest the refusal to authorise an assembly.

Law no. 560-XIII of 21 July 1995 regarding the organisation and conduct of assemblies provides under Section 15(2) that the relevant judicial body shall decide upon the organiser's contestation within 5 days from its lodging.

Section 34 of Law no. 123 of 18 March 2003 regarding local public administration provides that the Mayor undertakes legal measures regarding the conduct of public assemblies over the administered territory.

Section 34 of Law no. 123 of 18 March 2003 regarding local public administration provides that the Mayor undertakes measures forbidding or suspending shows, presentations and other public demonstrations which contradict legal order and morals.

Article 54(1) of the Moldovan Constitution provides that the exercise of certain rights or freedoms may be restricted only under the law and only as required for: the defence of national security, of public order, health or morals, of citizens' rights and freedoms, the carrying out of investigations in criminal cases, the prevention of the consequences of a natural calamity or of a technological disaster.
Article 54(2) of the Moldovan Constitution provides that restrictions enforced must be in proportion to the situation that caused them, and may not affect the existence of that right or liberty.

Article 184 of the Moldovan Civil Code defines an association as a non-commercial organisation established voluntarily by associated individuals and legal entities under provisions of the law on the basis of community of interests, which are consistent with public order and good morals, for the purpose of meeting various non-material needs.
